title: DevSuperSuite Enterprise Vendor Risk & CAIQ Compliance Matrix
summary: Standardized machine-readable database mapping 52 enterprise vendor risk questions across CSA CAIQ v4.0.2, Shared Assessments SIG Core v2024, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and AICPA SOC 2 Type II.

items.question: Are independent third-party audits of security controls conducted annually?
items.response: Yes. Independent SOC 2 Type II audits (Schellman/BDO) and CREST-accredited penetration tests (Bishop Fox/NCC Group) conducted annually with zero exceptions noted.
items.evidence: AICPA SOC 2 Type II Report FY2025-2026

items.question: Are audit trails maintained for all access to sensitive customer data?
items.response: DevSuperSuite does not ingest customer code on vendor infrastructure. Local append-only cryptographically hashed audit logs are maintained on workstation storage.
items.evidence: OmniKernel Local Audit Architecture Spec v5.2

items.question: How are local API endpoints protected against remote exploitation?
items.response: OmniKernel local daemon binds strictly to local loopback (127.0.0.1:8443) or UNIX domain sockets. Outbound non-loopback bindings are blocked at the OS kernel level.
items.evidence: Kernel eBPF Socket Filter Verification Log

items.question: Does the software prevent arbitrary shell command injection?
items.response: AgentShield enforces strict AST-constrained command whitelisting. Destructive terminal primitives are blocked at the OS wrapper boundary with POSIX Exit Code 126.

items.question: How does the application optimize context windows and prevent memory exhaustion?
items.response: In-process AVX-512 vector Tree-sitter parsers collapse method bodies into typed interface stubs, delivering an audited 83.51% token reduction in <1.4ms.

items.question: Are automated SAST, DAST, and SCA security scans integrated into the CI/CD pipeline?
items.response: Yes. Continuous CodeQL (SAST), Snyk (SCA), and libFuzzer dynamic fuzzing run on all pull requests, blocking builds with CVSS >= 7.0.

items.question: What are the vendor Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO)?
items.response: Runtime RPO is 0.00 seconds (local git repositories); runtime RTO is <60 seconds on replacement hardware using offline Ed25519 activation.

items.question: Does the vendor maintain source code escrow arrangements?
items.response: Yes. Master Software Escrow Agreement maintained with NCC Group and Iron Mountain, updated semi-annually with verified build manifests.

items.question: How frequently are disaster recovery and business continuity plans tested?
items.response: Tested semi-annually with full disaster simulation scenarios presented to the Executive Risk Committee.

items.question: Are validated cryptographic algorithms implemented?
items.response: FIPS 140-3 Level 3 compliant: Ed25519 asymmetric signatures, AES-256-GCM, and BLAKE3 / SHA-384. Zero legacy ciphers (no MD5, SHA-1, DES).

items.question: How are cryptographic keys generated, stored, and zeroized?
items.response: Keys reside in locked memory pages (mlock) and are zeroized via explicit_bzero. Persistent storage utilizes TPM 2.0, DPAPI, or Apple Secure Enclave.

items.question: What is the key rotation schedule for software licensing?
items.response: Release root keys rotated annually via HSM derivation; client offline public keys support multi-key concurrent validation.

items.question: Does the vendor ingest or train AI models on customer source code?
items.response: ABSOLUTELY NOT. Zero model training, zero cloud storage, zero telemetry egress. Source code is parsed strictly in transient local memory.
items.evidence: Zero Data Ingestion Warranty & SLA Schedule

items.question: How are transient in-memory AST buffers sanitized?
items.response: Transient volatile memory pages are locked against disk swap (mlock) and cryptographically zeroized (memset_s) upon session completion.

items.question: Does customer code cross sovereign national borders?
items.response: No. Local silicon execution guarantees code never leaves the workstation, eliminating cross-border data transfer concerns.

items.question: Does the software require root or elevated administrative privileges?
items.response: No. OmniKernel executes strictly in unprivileged user space without kernel extensions or process injection.

items.question: Can enterprise administrators deploy fleetwide configuration policies?
items.response: Yes. Centralized fleet_policy.toml deployment supported via Microsoft Intune, Jamf, and Ansible with tamper-evident checks.

items.question: Does the system support enterprise SAML 2.0 / OIDC authentication?
items.response: Yes. Administrative license management integrates with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and Ping Identity.

items.question: Is the software certified for air-gapped SCIF deployment?
items.response: Yes. Certified for air-gapped SCIF environments with unidirectional optical data diodes and offline Ed25519 validation.

items.question: Can OmniKernel execute within confidential computing enclaves?
items.response: Yes. Supports execution inside AWS Nitro Enclaves, Azure Confidential VMs (AMD SEV-SNP), and hardened containers.

items.question: What binary exploit mitigations are compiled into release artifacts?
items.response: Compiled with PIE (-fPIE), stack protection (-fstack-protector-strong), RELRO (-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now), and CFI.

items.question: What are the formal vulnerability remediation SLAs?
items.response: Critical (CVSS 9.0-10.0) patched within 48 hours; High (CVSS 7.0-8.9) patched within 7 calendar days.

items.question: Does the vendor maintain a Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) program?
items.response: Yes. Direct reporting via security@devsupersuite.com with published PGP keys and CVE numbering authority coordination.

items.question: How are third-party open source dependencies managed?
items.response: Locked with SHA-256 digests in Bazel manifests; scanned continuously against NVD via Snyk and Dependabot.

items.question: How does the software detect and intercept secrets in git repositories?
items.response: AgentShield hardware-accelerated Shannon entropy scan (H >= 4.50 bits/char) evaluates memory in <0.8ms, halting commits with POSIX Exit Code 1.

items.question: How does the software prevent autonomous agents from deleting unit tests?
items.response: AgentShield enforces INVARIANT_TEST_PRESERVATION at pre-commit hook level, blocking test deletions with POSIX Exit Code 2.

items.question: Does the software monitor host filesystem tampering?
items.response: Yes. Inotify/FSEvents notification watches detect unauthorized external modifications of local configuration manifests.

items.question: Provide vendor corporate solvency metrics and forward operating runway.
items.response: 37.5 months forward cash runway; Altman Z-Score of 4.86 (Safe Zone); 92.4% gross margin; zero long-term debt.

items.question: Detail commercial insurance limits and underwriting carriers.
items.response: $15M Cyber Liability (AIG/Lexington), $10M Tech E&O (Chubb), $4M General Liability (Travelers), $10M Umbrella.

items.question: Does the vendor maintain a formal, audited Information Security Management System?
items.response: Yes. Certified ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 27701:2019 ISMS audited annually by accredited registrars.

items.question: What data classification tiers can be processed securely?
items.response: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Highly Restricted / Secret data (including ITAR, CUI, and PHI).

items.question: How are enterprise cryptographic root keys established?
items.response: Rooted in host TPM 2.0 Platform Configuration Registers (PCR 0, 2, 4, 7) and offline Ed25519 public keys.

items.question: Detail build integrity and software supply chain verification standards.
items.response: SLSA Level 3 certified: hermetic Nix/Bazel builds, Sigstore Cosign binary signing, and CycloneDX v1.5 SBOM.

items.question: What is the security incident notification commitment?
items.response: Contractual commitment to notify enterprise clients within <24 hours of any confirmed security incident.

items.question: What happens if vendor cloud servers experience a multi-day outage?
items.response: Zero operational disruption. Client developer workstations operate 100% autonomously with offline Ed25519 license validation.

items.question: How are access control rules enforced on developer workstations?
items.response: Strict non-root user execution with central policy enforcement via signed fleet_policy.toml files.

items.question: How are cloud service risks mitigated for customer code?
items.response: Eliminated by design: DevSuperSuite maintains zero cloud code ingestion or cloud indexing servers.

items.question: How does the system prevent execution of destructive commands?
items.response: AgentShield command execution whitelist intercepts destructive shell primitives (rm -rf, mkfs) with POSIX Exit 126.

items.question: What data leakage prevention controls protect sensitive code?
items.response: AgentShield hardware SIMD Shannon entropy scan (H >= 4.50) halts staging of secrets with POSIX Exit Code 1.

items.question: How is network perimeter security verified for developer daemons?
items.response: Daemon binds strictly to local loopback (127.0.0.1); eBPF tracepoints verify 0.00 KB outbound network traffic.

items.question: What cryptographic standards govern local storage?
items.response: FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated cryptography: Ed25519, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, and BLAKE3.

items.question: How are secure coding invariants enforced against autonomous agents?
items.response: AgentShield INVARIANT_TEST_PRESERVATION blocks autonomous agents from deleting unit tests (POSIX Exit Code 2).

items.question: How is logical boundary protection maintained for customer data?
items.response: Customer code is parsed strictly in local workstation RAM. Zero customer code crosses machine boundaries.
items.evidence: SOC 2 Type II Report Section IV §CC6.1

items.question: How are data transmissions protected against unauthorized exfiltration?
items.response: Prompts route across private AWS PrivateLink or local on-premises models. OmniKernel transmits zero telemetry.
items.evidence: SOC 2 Type II Report Section IV §CC6.7

items.question: How are security vulnerabilities and credential exposures detected?
items.response: Real-time CPU SIMD Shannon entropy scanning intercepts secrets in RAM before staging or transmission.
items.evidence: SOC 2 Type II Report Section IV §CC7.1

items.question: What mechanisms guarantee operational availability during cloud outages?
items.response: Local silicon execution is 100% autonomous. Outages of public clouds or vendor servers cause zero disruption.
items.evidence: SOC 2 Type II Report Section IV §A1.1

items.question: How is customer confidential information protected and disposed of?
items.response: Zero data retention. Volatile memory buffers are locked against disk swap (mlock) and zeroized via explicit_bzero.
items.evidence: SOC 2 Type II Report Section IV §C1.1

items.question: How is information flow control enforced across security domains?
items.response: Full air-gap compliance. Operates across optical unidirectional data diodes with zero external network connectivity.

items.question: How are cryptographic keys established and managed?
items.response: Hardware-rooted in TPM 2.0 PCR registers and offline Ed25519 asymmetric signatures.

items.question: How does the software prevent unauthorized electronic PHI exfiltration?
items.response: In-memory AST sanitization strips 18 statutory HIPAA identifiers and clinical schemas before prompt assembly.

items.question: How is Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) protected from cloud exposure?
items.response: 100% US-owned entity (zero FOCI); certified for sovereign SCIF air-gapped enclaves with zero cloud telemetry.

items.question: How does the system ensure autonomous agents preserve safety-critical MC/DC test coverage?
items.response: AgentShield pre-commit AST delta analysis blocks deletion of MC/DC test fixtures with POSIX Exit Code 2.
